rounds.fact: Plenty of Fish was famously built and run by a single person for years, supported entirely by ads, before eventually being sold for hundreds of millions of dollars.
WebMD launched in 1996 and became so widely used for self-diagnosis that 'don't WebMD your symptoms' turned into a common joke about people convincing themselves they had rare diseases.
The Wall was a single editable text field in the earliest versions. 2007's platform launch brought app chaos, sheep-throwing included, before the News Feed took over the world.
Weather.com was one of the earliest sites to make hyper-local content practical on the web, letting visitors punch in a zip code long before that felt like a standard web feature.
Blizzard's late-90s site supported both Diablo and StarCraft, two games that helped define entire genres and whose online play features were unusually ambitious for their time.
